title: A WordPress pattern is read as the blocks it inserts, so a part the build expands to change its words keeps its structure
steps: S1: expandPatterns on a part holding only <!-- wp:pattern {"slug":"t/part-sidebar"} /-->, whose pattern holds a heading and another pattern; and on a reference the plugin cannot read.
S2: compareAgentInventory with the frozen part read expanded, against the part stored expanded with its words changed, and against it with one image block added.
S3: a frozen inventory read before patterns were (no patternsRead, the part as a reference) against an untouched part read expanded, with its reference kept as read.
expect: S1: both patterns are inlined; the unreadable reference stays as it was.
S2: changed words pass; the added block fails.
evidence: Local round 33 (26/10/2026, WordPress JA Restaurant): templatePart/sidebar was <!--wp:pattern/--> at install and its expanded blocks after the build changed 'Most Read'; native-structure failed it at checks 4 and 5.
fence: expandPatterns (PATTERN_REF, PATTERN_DEPTH, content.get {kind:"pattern"}); patternsRead marker; patternsAsRead for frozen inventories read before

tests: a pattern is read as the blocks it inserts: an expanded part keeps its structure, an added block does not
